title: Whistler's Mother's real title
hook: The painting known as Whistler's Mother is officially an arrangement in grey and black.
peek: Everyone calls it Whistler's Mother, but James McNeill Whistler titled his 1871 painting Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1. To him it was a study of colour and shape first, and a portrait of his mother second.
lede: It is one of the most recognised paintings in the world: an older woman in black, seated in profile against a grey wall. The sitter really was the painter's mother, Anna McNeill Whistler. But James McNeill Whistler gave it a cooler name, Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1. He wanted viewers to look at tones and shapes, not at family feeling.

bullets.text: Whistler liked to name his pictures like pieces of music: Nocturnes, Symphonies, Harmonies, Arrangements. He believed a painting should be enjoyed for its colours and forms, the way people enjoy a tune without asking what it means.

His mother is said to have stepped in when another model failed to arrive. The pose was first meant to be standing, but she found that too tiring, so Whistler painted her seated, which gives the picture its calm, settled feel.
In 1891 the French state bought the painting, the first work by an American artist to enter the national collection. It now hangs in the Musée d'Orsay in Paris.

In 1934 the United States issued a Mother's Day stamp based on the painting. That use helped turn Whistler's careful arrangement into a symbol of motherhood, the very reading its title tried to avoid.
